activities.anchor: a fourth quietly opens a job site
activities.caption: walk the four hearings of one sentence
activities.name: comSceneBranch

config.root: The manager says 'the project has been deprioritised.' The words travel perfectly. Walk the hearings.

start.text: One sentence, four listeners. What does the transmission model predict?

choices.label: One message, delivered intact — zero noise
choices.feedback: By the pipe: success. The word arrived with the signal unscrambled — and the meaning still went four directions at once.

choices.label: Four meanings, negotiated through four fields of experience
choices.feedback: Meaning-centred: each listener decodes through everything they have lived through — and only the overlap carries.

pipe.text: The pipe predicts delivery. The room delivers four different messages: cancelled, postponed, lost interest, résumé-polishing.

fields.text: Four fields, four decodings — and on the constitutive view the sentence did not describe the team's status; in that moment it was the team's status being made.

config.why: Success is shared interpretation, co-produced — which is why 'I told them' is not a defence.

activities.caption: put Shannon's 1948 assembly line in order
activities.name: comPipeOrder

config.prompt: Put Shannon's 1948 assembly line in order:
items: Source — the person with the idea
Encoder — turns the idea into signals that can travel
Channel — the road the signal travels, with noise scrambling it on the way
Decoder — turns the signal back into a message
Receiver — the person at the other end
config.why: How much information can get through a noisy channel, and how do codes beat noise? — the engineering question the drawing was built for.

activities.caption: fill the blanks — the two halves of a sign
activities.name: comSignCloze

config.text: Saussure split every sign into two halves: the signifier is the %%0%% half — mark, image, spoken shape — and the signified is the %%1%% half — the concept it calls up. The link between them is %%2%% and conventional: community agreement, not nature.
config.hint: One thumb, two cultures, opposite meanings — the pairing is learned.

activities.anchor: Charles Sanders Peirce sorted signs by
activities.caption: pair each kind with how it refers
activities.name: comPeirceMatch

config.prompt: Pair each kind with how it refers:

pairs.right: resembles what it shows — a photograph, a map
points by physical connection — smoke means fire, a fever means infection
rests on pure agreement — words, flags, most of culture

config.why: The split still organises media analysis today.

activities.anchor: Advertising is where you can watch the machinery running
activities.caption: file each layer under the tool that reads it
activities.name: comLayerSort

config.prompt: File each reading under the layer it belongs to:

items.label: a photograph of a man in a uniform
the improved-and-trustworthy feeling the word carries
freedom and desirability chained to the car

config.why: Myth is freight hardened into common sense — the third layer, Barthes' technical term for connotations that feel natural.

activities.anchor: it can be screenshotted in seconds
activities.caption: drag the divider across the affordances
activities.name: comAffordCompare

config.prompt: Same words, different channels — drag the divider:

before.label: spoken only
before.text: Cultures without writing remember and argue differently — formulaic, rhythmic, tied to particular situations — because the vanishing word shapes the habits of thought.

after.label: from letter to screenshot
after.text: A letter lasts a century; one screenshot makes a message permanent within a blink — scalable, searchable and editable besides.

config.why: Affordances are the practical difference between channels: same words, three different events — said aloud, emailed, leaked.

activities.anchor: as a law of history it overstates the case
activities.caption: true or false — how far the provocation goes
activities.name: comDeterminJudge

statements.s: Media cause social forms — and the claim holds unconditionally.
statements.why: Societies shape their media as much as media shape societies — the aphorism is a strong hypothesis, not an iron rule.

statements.s: The same television technology served totalitarian and democratic projects alike.
statements.why: The causation runs both directions — form reshapes communication, and societies shape their media back.

statements.s: Print fostered linear argument; television fostered spectacle and simultaneity.
statements.why: McLuhan radicalising Innis: media have biases — stone lasts but cannot travel, papyrus travels but fades.

statements.s: 'The medium is the message' means content does not matter.
statements.why: The claim is narrower: a medium's form reshapes communication independently of any particular content.

activities.caption: slide to the year of the settled middle ground
activities.name: comAgendaPlace

config.prompt: Effects research swung from injection to limited influence to influence without injection. Slide the marker to the year McCombs and Shaw published agenda setting.
config.why: 1972: media may not tell us what to think, but they powerfully tell us what to think about — the settled middle ground between injection and the earlier null findings.
